nodes.summary: For every Kripke model $M$, every environment $\rho$ (an assignment of a predicate on worlds to each variable index), every atom $p$ and every world $w$, the μ-calculus formula $\mathsf{AG}\,p$ holds at $w$ in $\rho$ if and only if $p$ is true at every world reachable from $w$ in zero or more steps of the accessibility relation of $M$.
nodes.title: $\mathsf{AG}$ is universal reachability

nodes.summary: For an atom $p$, $\mathsf{AG}\,p$ is the greatest fixed point formula $\nu X.\,(p \wedge \Box X)$. It expresses that every state reachable from the current one satisfies $p$.
nodes.title: The μ-calculus formula $\mathsf{AG}\,p$

nodes.summary: A formula is closed at depth `d` when every free de Bruijn variable is `< d`: only `μ` / `ν` increase the depth; `□` / `◇` do not bind variables and preserve it.
nodes.title: μ-calculus formula closed at a given binding depth

nodes.summary: A formula is closed when it is closed at depth `0`: every variable is bound.
nodes.title: Closed modal μ-calculus formula

nodes.summary: For every predicate $S$ on worlds, the predicate $w \mapsto \neg\neg S(w)$ equals $S$.
nodes.title: Double complement of a predicate

nodes.summary: A formula's depth is at most its code: pairing dominates each component (`Nat.add_le_pair`).
nodes.title: Depth of a μ-calculus formula is at most its number code

nodes.summary: The depth of a formula: the length of its longest root-to-leaf path, counting each connective once.
nodes.title: Depth of a modal μ-calculus formula

nodes.summary: For every Kripke model $M$, every environment $\rho$ (an assignment of a predicate on worlds to each variable index), every atom $p$ and every world $w$, the μ-calculus formula $\mathsf{EF}\,p$ holds at $w$ in $\rho$ if and only if $p$ is true at some world reachable from $w$ in zero or more steps of the accessibility relation of $M$.
nodes.title: $\mathsf{EF}$ is reachability

nodes.summary: For an atom $p$, $\mathsf{EF}\,p$ is the least fixed point formula $\mu X.\,(p \vee \Diamond X)$. It expresses that some state reachable from the current one satisfies $p$.
nodes.title: The μ-calculus formula $\mathsf{EF}\,p$

nodes.summary: For every environment $\rho$ (assigning to each variable index $n$ a predicate $\rho(n)$ on worlds) and every predicate $S$ on worlds, complementing every predicate of the extension of $\rho$ by $S$ gives the extension of the complemented environment $n \mapsto \neg\rho(n)$ by the predicate $w \mapsto \neg S(w)$.
nodes.title: Complementing an extended environment

nodes.summary: An environment $\rho$ assigns to each variable index $n \in \mathbb{N}$ a predicate $\rho(n)$ on worlds. Its extension by a predicate $S$ on worlds is the environment that assigns $S$ to index $0$ and $\rho(n)$ to index $n + 1$.
nodes.title: Extending an environment under a binder

nodes.summary: The encoding is injective.
nodes.title: Injectivity of the μ-calculus number code

nodes.summary: An injective encoding of μ-calculus formulas over `ℕ` atoms as natural numbers, via the Cantor pairing function `Nat.pair`. This is a Nat code only, not a complexity input encoding: repeated pairing squares the code at every unary connective, so the binary length of the code of `box^d (atom 0)` doubles at each `box` and is exponential in `d`. Complexity statements use `muTokens` / `muDecodeList` instead.
nodes.title: Cantor-pairing number code of a μ-calculus formula

nodes.summary: Decoding inverts encoding, with enough fuel: a formula's own code carries more fuel than its depth needs.
nodes.title: Fuelled decoding inverts the μ-calculus number code

nodes.summary: Fuelled decoding of a `muCode` number back to a formula. The fuel bounds the recursion depth; `muDecode` supplies fuel `c + 1`, which exceeds every formula's depth (see `depth_le_code`).
nodes.title: Fuelled decoding of a μ-calculus number code

nodes.summary: Decoding inverts token encoding.
nodes.title: Token-list decoding inverts modal μ-calculus token encoding

nodes.summary: Decoding inverts encoding.
nodes.title: Decoding inverts the μ-calculus number code

nodes.summary: Decode a `muCode` number back to the formula it encodes.
nodes.title: Decoding a μ-calculus number code to a formula

nodes.summary: The formulas over a type of atoms are built from atoms $a$, negated atoms $\neg a$, variables $X_n$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$ (de Bruijn indices for the fixed-point binders), $\bot$ and $\top$ by conjunction $\varphi \wedge \psi$, disjunction $\varphi \vee \psi$, the modalities $\Box\varphi$ and $\Diamond\varphi$, and the fixed-point binders $\mu\varphi$ and $\nu\varphi$.
nodes.title: Formulas of the modal μ-calculus

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model, $\rho$ an environment, $\varphi$ a μ-calculus formula and $P$ a predicate on worlds. If every world satisfying $\varphi$ in the extension of $\rho$ by $P$ satisfies $P$, then every world satisfying $\mu\varphi$ in $\rho$ satisfies $P$.
nodes.title: Park induction

nodes.summary: For every Kripke model $M$, environment $\rho$ and μ-calculus formula $\varphi$, every world satisfying $\mu\varphi$ in $\rho$ also satisfies $\varphi$ in the extension of $\rho$ by the set of worlds satisfying $\mu\varphi$ in $\rho$.
nodes.title: The least fixed point is contained in its unfolding

nodes.summary: For every Kripke model $M$ and every environment $\rho$, the formula $\mu X.\, \mu Y.\, X$ holds at no world of $M$ under $\rho$. In de Bruijn form this formula is $\mu\, \mu\, x_1$: inside the inner binder, variable $1$ refers to the outer binder, not to the inner one.
nodes.title: The formula $\mu X.\, \mu Y.\, X$ is false everywhere

nodes.summary: Given a Kripke model $M$, an environment $\rho$ (a set of worlds $\rho(n)$ for each variable $n$) and a μ-calculus formula $\varphi$, this is the monotone map on sets of worlds of $M$ sending $S$ to the set of worlds at which $\varphi$ holds under $\rho[S]$, the extension of $\rho$ under a binder by $S$ (variable $0$ denotes $S$ and variable $n + 1$ denotes $\rho(n)$).
nodes.title: The fixed-point operator of a formula

nodes.summary: Parsing inverts token encoding, with enough fuel.
nodes.title: Fuelled parsing inverts modal μ-calculus token encoding

nodes.summary: Fuelled parsing of a `muTokens` token list back to a formula, returning the formula and the unconsumed suffix. The fuel bounds the recursion depth; `muDecodeList` supplies fuel `l.length + 1`.
nodes.title: Fuelled parser for modal μ-calculus token lists

nodes.summary: A closed formula does not depend on the environment: environments agreeing below the depth give the same denotation.
nodes.title: Denotation of a closed μ-calculus formula is environment-independent

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a Kripke model and let $\rho$ and $\rho'$ be environments (each assigns a set of worlds of $M$ to every variable $n$) with $\rho(n) \subseteq \rho'(n)$ for every $n$. Then every μ-calculus formula $\varphi$ holds under $\rho'$ at every world of $M$ where it holds under $\rho$: enlarging every variable's denotation can only enlarge a formula's denotation.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
